data.name: Huzaimah
data.long_meaning: في اللغة العربية، اسم حُزَامَة يعكس معاني الشجاعة والعزيمة والأمل. يُفضل استخدامه لأسماء الأطفال المسلمين ويُشجع القيم العربية والإسلامية.

in_arabic.name: حزامة
in_arabic.long_meaning: حزامة اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي ويحمل معنى القوة والشجاعة، مستوحى من الكلمة العربية حزام، ولهذا الاسم أهمية دينية وثقافية في التقاليد الإسلامية حيث يركز على القوة الروحية والاجتماعية

in_urdu.name: حزامہ
in_urdu.meaning: مضبوط و قوی خواتین کا نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: حزامہ ایک عربي نام ہے جو قوتی اور مضبوطی کی علامت ہے، یہ نام برصغیر پاک و ہند میں اسلامی روایات میں خاص مقام رکھتا ہے اور خواتین کی روحانی و سماجی قوت کا پرچم ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name Huzaimah holds a beautiful connection to nature, as it is derived from the Arabic word "hawz" which means "garden" or "source of water". In the Islamic context, this name holds deep cultural significance as it refers to someone who is constantly nurturing and blooming like a beautiful garden. It is an evocative name that reflects the love and appreciation for the natural world and the concept of growth and development.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Huzaimah holds a deeper meaning as it represents someone who is in a state of continuous growth and development, like a garden that is tended and nurtured. In Islamic teachings, this name is used as a reminder to always strive for self-improvement, to cultivate one's character and soul, and to seek knowledge and wisdom like a lifetime source of water. It is a name that inspires us to live a meaningful and fulfilling life, always in pursuit of growth and progress, both in this world and in the hereafter.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End) - Volume 7 The name Huzaimah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: One of the Ansar (Helpers) of Madinah who embraced Islam early. He was known as Huzaifah bin Al-Yaman, but he was called Huzaimah after the migration to Madinah. He was the cousin of Ali ibn Abi Talib and the standard-bearer of Ali's army during the Battle of Uhud.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tabari's Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk (History of Prophets and Kings) - Volume 5 The name Huzaimah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Huzaimah ibn Hizam was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He was a man of great wealth and was among the first to embrace Islam. When the Muslims migrated from Mecca to Medina, Huzaimah was among those who were given the title 'Al-Ashiq al-Abi' (The Loving Old Man), due to his advanced age and his deep love for the Prophet and Islam.
